newsitem.title: FINLAND: NESTE FOUR-MONTH PROFITS STEADY, 1997 EARNINGS SEEN UP.
newsitem.headline: NESTE FOUR-MONTH PROFITS STEADY, 1997 EARNINGS SEEN UP.

text.p: Finnish oil and energy group Neste Oy on Wednesday reported steady January-April profits but said it expected full-year 1997 earnings to improve on 1996 when it had operating profits of 1.08 billion markka ($209.7 million).

"Despite uncertainty in respect of the crude price and other market prices there is reason to believe that overall, Neste's operating profit for 1997 will improve on 1996," it said in its four-month interim report.

Neste's forecast for improved 1997 profits was based on a crude oil price estimate of $18 per barrel, Neste's chief financial officer Eero Aittola told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in an interview.
Neste reported January-April profits before extraordinary items of 214 million markka, little changed from the 219 million markka booked in the same period last year.
But the result was well below analysts' forecasts which had been for a median profit of 431 million markka in a 233-600 million markka range in a Reuters poll.
On the Helsinki bourse on Wednesday afternoon, Neste's share traded at 134.00 markka, down 3.50, but off a session low of 131.00 in very thin 1.6 million markka volume.
Earnings per share for the first four months rose to 1.90 markka from 1.65 markka. Net sales were up slightly at 14.69 billion markka from 14.41 billion.
Operating profits improved at Neste's exploration and production and energy divisions, while performances by its chemicals division and oil division weakened.

"The main reason (for the decline in earnings) was that we booked an inventory loss of about 250 million markka," Aittola told RFTV, adding that the losses came on oil stocks of some one million tonnes which Neste is required to keep by law.
Neste does not hedge against the risks of those inventories, which remain exposed to fluctuations in crude oil prices, Aittola said.
"We don't hedge those because we expect the fluctuations to even out in the long term," Aittola said.
After 1996 oil trading losses of 560 million markka cut into earnings, Neste has downsized its trading operations this year.
"The current volume (of trading) measured by turnover is 1.5 billion markka less than in the same period of the previous year," Aittola said.
Oil trading activities contributed 4.27 billion markka to four-month net sales, versus 5.61 billion in the same period last year, Neste said in the report.
Neste said progress had been made in negotations on the sale of its 50 percent holding in petrochemicals group Borealis, which it owns together with Statoil of Norway. It did not elaborate.
